The guide builds its case on rarity — returning the conference's Offensive Player of the Year, at quarterback, plus a 1,000-yard back — and treats the Broncos as expected to make a strong run at repeating. Its honest accounting of how the wins came is that Western Michigan managed only 5.2 yards per play, helped by a +9 turnover margin, with a defense it calls spectacular.
